q: Among the road classifications set by BP 220 and PD 957, which one is the narrowest?
n: An alley is 2.0 m wide, narrower than a 3.0 m pathwalk or any road; it only breaks long blocks and may not serve as lot access.

q: What is the maximum riser height BP 220 allows for stairs?
n: BP 220 limits stair risers to 0.25 m, with treads of at least 0.20 m.

q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum tread width required for stairs?
n: BP 220 requires stair treads of at least 0.20 m, paired with a riser of no more than 0.25 m.

q: Among these housing classifications, which one commands the highest cost?
n: Open market housing is the top price bracket under PD 957; medium cost sits below it, and economic and socialized housing (BP 220) lower still.

q: Which of the following is NOT permitted under BP 220 and PD 957?
o: A rowhouse cluster 100 m long with 20 units
A block 250 m long with no alley at all
A block 500 m long with a 2 m mid-block alley
A block 400 m long with a 2 m mid-block alley
n: Blocks may not exceed 400 m, alley or not; a 2 m alley is needed only once a block passes 250 m, and rowhouse clusters stop at 20 units or 100 m.

q: At what block length does an alley become required?
n: Blocks may run up to 400 m, but any block longer than 250 m needs a 2 m alley near mid-length.

q: What saleable-to-non-saleable lot area ratio does BP 220 mandate?
n: Remember: there is no prescribed ratio in BP 220.

q: What saleable-to-non-saleable lot area ratio does PD 957 mandate?
n: Remember: PD 957 only caps the saleable portion, and only places a minimum for the non-saleable portion.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: An alley must have a minimum width of 1.20 m.
An alley may be used as property access for socialized developments only
A pathwalk length of up to 60.00 m. is allowed
A pathwalk may be used as property access for socialized and economic developments
n: A pathwalk of up to 60.00 m. is allowed. The other statements are wrong: an alley must be at least 2.00 m. wide, not 1.20 m.; an alley may never be used as access to a property, for any type of project; and a pathwalk may serve as property access only in socialized projects, not economic ones.

q: Excluding mezzanines, what is the minimum ceiling height required for socialized and economic housing?
n: BP 220 sets a 2.00 m minimum ceiling height for habitable rooms of socialized and economic housing, and 1.80 m above and below a mezzanine.

q: What is the smallest door size that BP 220 allows?
n: This is theoretically allowed for bathroom doors.

q: What range of handrail heights is acceptable under BP 220?
n: BP 220 handrails go no lower than 0.80 m and no higher than 1.20 m above the tread.

q: For socialized single-detached housing, what is the minimum lot frontage required?
n: BP 220 Table 8 gives socialized single-detached lots an 8 m minimum frontage.

q: What is the minimum front setback required for socialized and economic housing?
n: Economic and socialized houses need a 1.5 m front setback, 1.5 m side yard and 2.0 m rear yard.

q: At what minimum gross project area do parks and playgrounds become a requirement?
n: Parks and playgrounds are mandatory for projects of 1 hectare or more, sized by density.

q: Which of the following structures may be built on land set aside for parks and playgrounds?
n: Park and playground land stays open and recreational; a basketball court fits, while clinics and centers are community facilities placed elsewhere.

q: Which three items head BP 220's list of the minimum basic needs of human settlements?
o: Water, parks and playgrounds, and circulation
n: BP 220 ranks basic needs: water first, then movement and circulation, storm drainage, waste disposal, parks and playgrounds, and power last.

q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum floor area required for a single-occupancy open market condominium unit?
n: PD 957 condominium rules give single-occupancy units at least 18 sqm (12 sqm net may be allowed).

q: For medium-cost and open market subdivisions with a density of 20 lots or dwelling units per hectare or less, what percentage of the gross area must be allocated to parks and playgrounds?
n: For 20 or fewer lots or units per hectare (low density), 3.5% of the gross area goes to parks and playgrounds; 9% applies to high density.

q: What is the minimum required floor area for open market housing?
n: PD 957 sets 42 sqm as the minimum floor area for open market housing and 30 sqm for medium cost.

q: What is the minimum level of completion PD 957 requires for a housing unit?
o: Shell house with doors and windows
n: This is not low-cost housing. At the price points in PD 957, shell houses are not allowed.

q: What is the minimum lot area required for medium cost duplex housing?
n: PD 957 Table 6 gives medium cost duplexes an 80 sqm minimum lot area; open market duplexes need 96 sqm.

q: Under BP 220, how far must a firewall extend above the roof line at minimum?
n: Firewalls must rise at least 0.30 m above the highest point of the roof they adjoin and extend 0.30 m beyond it horizontally.

q: For subdivisions fronting main public roads, what are the minimum dimensions of the setback required on both sides of the entrance for public utility vehicles?
n: Subdivisions on main public roads must leave setbacks of at least 3.0 m × 5.0 m on both sides of the entrance for PUVs to load and unload.

q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum floor area required for a medium cost family condominium unit?
n: Medium cost family condominium units need at least 22 sqm; open market family units need 36 sqm.
